edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. I, 10

source_text: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te. Si vis intellegere, o sponsa, quomodo scire te debeas, cognosce, cui te comparaverim, et tunc videbis talem te esse, quae turpari non debeas, cum tuam speciem recognoveris. Quid est igitur: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te? Scio ego equitem sponsum propheta dicente: Et equitatio eius salus. Assimilata es ergo equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis. Quanto differt equitatus meus, qui sum Dominus — equos eius et currus eius — quanto, inquam, differt equitatus meus ab equis Pharaonis, tanto tu melior es omnibus filiabus, tu sponsa, tu ecclesiastica anima, omnibus animabus, quae non sunt ecclesiasticae. Igitur si ecclesiastica anima es, omnibus animabus es melior. Deinde pulchritudinem sponsae spiritali amore describit: Genae tuae sicut turturis. Collum tuum sicut monilia.
pass_a_gloss: To cavalry of-me in chariots of-Pharaoh I-likened you. If you-wish to-understand how you-ought to-know yourself, learn to-whom I-compared you; then see you ought-not be-disfigured once you recognize your form. Prophet: And his riding is salvation. As far as my cavalry (I the Lord) differs from Pharaoh's horses, so far you bride / churchly soul better than all non-churchly souls. Then describes beauty: Cheeks yours as of-turtledove; neck yours as necklaces.
notes: Pass A literalist gloss ≠ Pass B literary English.
Song lemma sense-checked against Baehrens; Lawson ACW not used for wording.
pass_b_english: [[I have likened you to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:9]]. If you wish to understand, O Bride, how you ought to know yourself, learn to whom I have compared you, and then you will see that you are such as ought not to be disfigured, once you recognize your own beauty. What then is this: I have likened you to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots? I know the Bridegroom as a rider, the prophet saying: [[And his riding is salvation >> Bible:Habakkuk 3:8]]. You have been likened, then, to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots. As far as my cavalry differs — I who am the Lord, his horses and his chariots — as far, I say, as my cavalry differs from Pharaoh’s horses, so far are you better than all daughters, you the Bride, you the churchly soul, better than all souls that are not churchly. Therefore if you are a churchly soul, you are better than all souls. Then he describes the Bride’s beauty with spiritual love: [[Your cheeks are like a turtledove’s >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:10]]. Your neck is like necklaces.
